title: eval-harness: per-prompt regression CI hook + quality gating for prompt sets
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Add a per-prompt regression CI hook and a lightweight quality-gating config for eval-harness prompt sets. Motivation: teams keep hitting regressions when adding or editing prompt sets; running the full eval locally is slow and noisy. This PR introduces a fast CI hook that runs a targeted subset of eval metrics per-prompt and enforces configurable thresholds so PRs fail fast when a prompt change causes quality regressions.

What changed (single list): - New CI hook workflow (ci/workflows/eval-harness-per-prompt.yml) that is triggered on pull_request and runs per-prompt checks scoped to changed prompt files. - New CLI helper (eval-harness/ci/per_prompt_hook.py) that: identifies changed prompt files, runs a small eval subset (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity thresholds), and emits machine-readable results for the workflow. - Gating config (eval-harness/config/gating.yaml) that exposes per-prompt thresholds and severity (warning/blocking). - Integration shim with metrics service (eval-harness/metrics/emit_hook.py) to record per-prompt CI metrics to Dataplane for dashboards and historical drift detection. - Tests: unit tests for CLI logic and an integration test that runs a small fake-model harness in CI. - Docs: docs/eval-harness/per-prompt-ci.md with usage, troubleshooting and how to configure thresholds.

Checklist: - [x] CLI and workflow implemented - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Documentation - [x] Metrics emission - [x] Non-breaking to existing eval flows

Notes on safety and scope: the hook runs only on changed prompt files by default and uses cached model artifacts to keep run-time under ~3 minutes on CI. Team can opt-in to stricter gating via gating.yaml.

Backwards compatibility: default gating is non-blocking (warning) to avoid breaking extant pipelines.

discussion: Jonah Kim (reviewer): Overall this looks good. Two asks: (1) add an opt-out label for repos that don't want CI gating, (2) add a short-circuit path when no numeric metrics are configured. Also can we measure CI runtime impact?

Maya Patel (author): Added repo opt-out support via gating.yaml 'enabled: false' and added short-circuit when thresholds are empty. CI runtime note: added cache step that reduces wall time from ~7m to ~2.5m on our runners (see CI checks).
Leila Garcia (reviewer): Please add an integration test that exercises a failing threshold so we lock the behavior. Also request small doc blurb about tuning thresholds for noisy prompts.
